title: Longest Run of Equal Values
statement: You are given n integers. A run is a block of equal values that sit next to each other. For example, in 1 1 2 2 2 1, the runs are 1 1, then 2 2 2, then 1. Print the length of the longest run.
inputFormat: First line: integer n. Second line: n space-separated integers.
outputFormat: Print one integer: the length of the longest run of equal consecutive values.
explanations: The runs are 1 1, then 2 2 2, then 1. The longest has length 3.
All five values are equal, so the whole list is one run of length 5.
reference:
import sys
data = sys.stdin.read().split()
n = int(data[0])
a = data[1:1 + n]
a = [int(x) for x in a]
best = 1
cur = 1
for i in range(1, n):
    if a[i] == a[i - 1]:
        cur += 1
    else:
        cur = 1
    if cur > best:
        best = cur
print(best)
